name: RabbitMQ
summary: Open-source message broker supporting AMQP and other protocols with flexible routing.
use_cases: Decoupling services, task queues, routing messages between producers and consumers.
tradeoffs: A stateful broker to operate and monitor.
Not designed for long-term event replay like a log-based system.
avoid_if: you need event replay or very high-throughput streaming.

name: Apache Kafka
summary: Distributed event streaming platform built on a durable, partitioned log.
use_cases: High-throughput event pipelines, event sourcing, stream processing, data integration.
avoid_if: you are a small team that just needs background jobs.

name: BullMQ
summary: Redis-backed job and message queue library for Node.js with retries, delays and repeatable jobs.
use_cases: Background jobs, scheduled tasks and rate-limited work in TypeScript backends.
tradeoffs: Durability is bounded by Redis persistence settings.
avoid_if: you cannot run Redis or need multi-language consumers at scale.

name: Celery
summary: Distributed task queue for Python using brokers such as RabbitMQ or Redis.
use_cases: Background jobs and periodic tasks in Django/FastAPI/Flask applications.
tradeoffs: Requires a separate broker and worker processes.

name: Amazon SQS
summary: Fully managed message queue service on AWS with standard and FIFO queues and dead-letter queues.
use_cases: Decoupling services on AWS, serverless pipelines with Lambda, buffering work.
tradeoffs: No built-in pub/sub fan-out (pair with SNS).
avoid_if: you must self-host or avoid a single cloud provider.

name: Temporal
summary: Durable execution platform: workflows written as code survive failures and retry automatically.
use_cases: Long-running business processes, payment flows, orchestrating many services or AI agents reliably.
tradeoffs: Self-hosting the cluster is a serious operational commitment.
Workflow code must follow determinism rules.
avoid_if: you only need simple fire-and-forget jobs.
